meta.note: 生活空间 sentence library; distractors are drawn at runtime from the target's 组别 (PATCH_02 §1) — none are stored here

phrases.en: This is our school.
The teacher is coming!
May I please go to the toilet?
This is my classmate.
He is my good friend.
The library has many books.
I use a pen to write my homework.
This is my tablet.
We have a Chinese test tomorrow.
I like my school.
I take the bus to school every day.
The bus stop is over there.
I take the MRT to the swimming pool.
I take a taxi to Orchard Road.

phrases.zh: 新加坡的樟宜机场很大。
phrases.en: Singapore's Changi Airport is very big.

phrases.zh: 我从新加坡搭飞机去上海。
phrases.en: I fly from Singapore to Shanghai.
I wait for my friend at the bus stop.
I like riding double-decker buses.
This is the bus interchange.
phrases.insight_en: An interchange is where many bus routes terminate and passengers change lines. Most are attached to an MRT station.

phrases.zh: 我的同学每天骑脚踏车上学。
phrases.en: My classmate cycles to school every day.
accepted_zh: 每天我的同学骑脚踏车上学

phrases.en: I want to buy a piece of clothing.
These shoes look very nice.
Excuse me, how much is this phone?
I bought an umbrella.
This handbag is very expensive.
My spectacles are broken.
I want to buy a highlighter.
The food court is on the third floor.
phrases.insight_en: A food court is the air-conditioned indoor cousin of a hawker centre, usually on an upper floor of a mall. Same stall-by-stall ordering, higher prices.

phrases.en: Let's go shopping together!
The fish here is very fresh.
I want to buy two tomatoes.
Excuse me, how much are ten eggs?
I want to buy a whole chicken.
I bought six crabs.

phrases.zh: 菜市场的菜比超级市场便宜。
phrases.en: Vegetables at the wet market are cheaper than at the supermarket.
Excuse me, how much is a packet of chillies?
This stall sells all kinds of spices.
Mum wants to buy two napa cabbages.
I want to buy four blocks of beancurd.
I want to buy a bottle of water.
I bought two pieces of bread.
How much is this packet of sweets?
I want to buy a bottle of coffee.
I want to buy a carton of juice.
This slice of cake is delicious.
Excuse me, how much is one bun?

phrases.zh: 今天很热，我想吃冰淇淋。
phrases.en: It's hot today, I want to eat ice cream.
This is an umbrella.
I don't need the receipt, thank you.
I'd like a plate of chicken rice to take away.
phrases.insight_en: 打包 (da bao) is the everyday word for takeaway in Singapore and Malaysia — you will hear it used in English conversation too.

phrases.en: I'd like to order a bowl of fish soup.
phrases.insight_en: You order and pay at each stall separately. There is no single central till.

phrases.en: This bowl of noodles is very hot — be careful!
I like eating curry chicken.
phrases.insight_en: Curry chicken shows how food travels between Singapore's communities: Indian in origin, cooked in Chinese, Malay and Indian households, each with its own version.

phrases.en: Is there a vegetarian stall here?
phrases.insight_en: Most hawker centres have a vegetarian stall, for Buddhist, Hindu or personal reasons. Halal stalls are separately certified and keep their own crockery and washing area, so Muslim customers can eat safely at the same centre.

phrases.en: I'd like an iced Milo.
phrases.insight_en: Milo is a malted chocolate drink most Singaporean children grow up on. Ask for a Milo dinosaur and you get it heaped with undissolved Milo powder.

phrases.en: I'd like a kopi-o — black coffee — with less sugar.
phrases.insight_en: Local coffee has its own ordering code borrowed from Hokkien. 乌 (o) means black. Condensed milk is the default unless you say otherwise, and 咖啡乌 already comes sweetened, which is why you must say 少糖 for less. Say 咖啡乌空 (kopi-o kosong) for none at all.

phrases.zh: 这里的果汁比商场便宜。
phrases.en: The juice here is cheaper than at the mall.
phrases.insight_en: Hawker centre rents are regulated, which is why the same drink costs less here than in a mall.

phrases.zh: 新加坡人习惯用纸巾占位子。
phrases.en: Singaporeans have a habit of using a packet of tissue to reserve a seat.
phrases.insight_en: Known in Singlish as choping. A tissue packet on a table means the seat is taken while you queue. It relies entirely on mutual trust and no one polices it.

phrases.zh: 吃完饭后，我们要归还碗盘。
phrases.en: After eating, we return our bowls and plates.
phrases.insight_en: Returning your tray became mandatory at hawker centres in 2021. Enforcement details have shifted since, so treat this as the habit rather than the letter of the rule.

phrases.zh: 我住在这座组屋的八楼。
phrases.en: I live on the eighth floor of this HDB block.
phrases.insight_en: HDB flats house about eight in ten Singaporeans. Stating your floor is a normal way to say where you live.

phrases.zh: 我忘记带钥匙，开不了门。
phrases.en: I forgot my keys and can't open the door.

phrases.zh: 电梯坏了，我们走楼梯吧！
phrases.en: The lift is broken — let's take the stairs!
My neighbour keeps a cat.

phrases.zh: 我家楼下有一个游乐场。
phrases.en: There is a playground downstairs from my home.

phrases.zh: 妈妈在走廊种了几盆花。
phrases.en: Mum grows several pots of flowers along the corridor.
phrases.insight_en: Corridor gardening is a real and slightly contested habit: residents line the common corridor with potted plants.

phrases.en: There is a fitness corner near my home.
phrases.insight_en: Fitness corners are free outdoor exercise stations built into most estates, used mainly by older residents in the early morning.

phrases.en: This is the community club.
phrases.insight_en: Community clubs run classes, festivals and activities for residents of every background, a deliberate instrument of Singapore's integration policy.

phrases.zh: 老人家在组屋底层下棋。
phrases.en: The elderly play chess on the ground floor of the block.
phrases.insight_en: The void deck, the open ground floor left empty under every block, hosts chess, weddings and funerals alike. Shared ground in the most literal sense.

phrases.en: There are many facilities in an HDB estate.
That monkey is climbing a tree.

phrases.zh: 小朋友可以在这里喂羊和兔子。
phrases.en: Children can feed the goats and rabbits here.
phrases.insight_en: The children's section lets visitors feed and touch farm animals. It is where most Singaporean children first meet a goat.
accepted_zh: 小朋友可以在这里喂兔子和羊

phrases.en: The lion's roar is terrifying!

phrases.zh: 我们一家人去动物园玩。
phrases.en: Our whole family goes to the zoo.
The elephant is drinking water — so cute!
These two tigers are sleeping.
Pandas like eating bamboo best.

phrases.zh: 晚上我们去夜间野生动物园玩。
phrases.en: At night we go to the Night Safari.
phrases.insight_en: The Night Safari was the world's first nocturnal zoo.

phrases.zh: 这里有许多珍稀的动物。
phrases.en: There are many rare animals here.

phrases.zh: 孩子们都喜欢参观动物园。
phrases.en: Children all like visiting the zoo.

phrases.zh: 我们一家人去农场参观。
phrases.en: Our whole family visits a farm.
phrases.insight_en: Singapore imports the overwhelming majority of its food and has very few working farms left, mostly around Kranji and Lim Chu Kang. Visiting one is a school excursion rather than an everyday sight.
accepted_zh: 我们一家人去参观农场

phrases.en: That horse runs very fast!
The farmer is feeding the cows and chickens.
This cow is eating grass.

phrases.zh: 我们去圣淘沙的海洋馆参观。
phrases.en: We visit the aquarium on Sentosa.
phrases.insight_en: The S.E.A. Aquarium on Sentosa is among the largest in the world. Sentosa is reached by cable car, monorail or boardwalk, so the journey is part of the outing.
accepted_zh: 我们去参观圣淘沙的海洋馆

phrases.en: I like watching the jellyfish swim.
That sea turtle swims very slowly.

phrases.zh: 我第一次看到这么大的龙虾。
phrases.en: It's my first time seeing such a big lobster.

phrases.zh: 在海洋馆不可以敲玻璃。
phrases.en: You mustn't tap the glass at the aquarium.
phrases.insight_en: Tapping the glass startles the animals. Most Singaporean children are told this on their first visit, so it doubles as an etiquette lesson.
accepted_zh: 不可以在海洋馆敲玻璃

phrases.en: That shark is so fierce!

phrases.zh: 这里有许多五颜六色的热带鱼。
phrases.en: There are many colourful tropical fish here.
